Ollama health-flap root cause + fix. Symptom: /api/health/health intermittently reported BOTH adapters offline (~2/10 probes, both together, fast, no error) while top-level status stayed healthy and chat/inference worked (OLLAMA_CHAT_OK verified end-to-end via POST /api/integrations/ollama/chat with gemma4:e2b-it-qat). Root cause: main.py health_broadcast_loop mutated the SHARED cached dict returned by get_aggregate_health() - it set adapter status healthy->online in place; the /api/health endpoint then re-maps status with (online if status==healthy else offline), so the already-mapped online reads as offline. Any probe landing in the 2s cache window after a 5s broadcast therefore reported healthy adapters as offline. Fix: build a copy for broadcasting instead of mutating the cache (main.py health_broadcast_loop). Verified: 12/12 probes online after watchfiles hot-reload (new uvicorn worker PID), type+lint gates PASS, chat still OLLAMA_CHAT_OK. Third turn: implemented the remix iteration plan's deliberately-parked list (owner asked; three of four landed, wizard stays parked with its reasoning). Design points worth keeping. (1) Cancel: the job hands its worker the cancel token (a zero-arg callable) rather than the caller guessing a job id before the thread starts - that closes a real race and needed no signature guessing; the mix being entirely in memory is what makes cancel non-destructive (nothing written, previous render intact), so a cancelled build is not a destructive one. Non-cancellable kinds are refused 409 rather than accepted and never observed - an enhance accepted-then-ignored would sit in cancelling until the timeout, which is a wedge dressed up as a feature. (2) Version history: archive the whole directory (stems+manifest+enhanced), and keep it under a dot-directory so the existing list (which skips dot entries) needs no change; an unknown version 404s rather than silently serving the current render. (3) A/B: pins are structural snapshots, and the which-variant-am-I marker is equality with the pin, never a last-loaded flag - a flag lies after the first edit. E2E traps hit and fixed: the timeline segments are <button role="option"> whose accessible names collide with stem play buttons (use exact names); and detached new Audio() playback leaves no DOM trace AND no Playwright request event, so assert via a HTMLMediaElement.prototype.play spy plus the element's currentSrc/readyState (that probe proved the panel was correct and the assertion was wrong - measured readyState 4, error null, currentSrc the versioned URL). Repo conventions confirmed: custom exceptions carry the Error suffix (ruff N818); the backend's watchfiles locks a file for a few seconds after a reload, so retry the write rather than concluding the file is unwritable; when inserting a Playwright test before another, match the whole declaration line or you clobber the following test (done twice, fixed twice).
